This is a thorough explanation of what bullying is, and why bullying is bad and hurtful to other people. The purpose is to prevent someone else from bullying another person within this community, and to help them to understand why bullying is very bad and hurtful to do that on the internet, as well as in the real world.

What bullying is

:3HC_PinkDot: Verbal bullying- this involves saying or writing mean things.

1. Name calling
2. Teasing someone in a hurtful way
3. Making fun of someone
4. Being sarcastic in a hurtful way
5. Offensive comments, insults or jokes about someone and their family because of their race, culture, religion, disability or sexuality
6. Mean comments about someone's body or physical characteristics such as their weight or height
7. Hurtful comments about the way someone looks or behaves
8. Inappropriate sexual comments
9. Taunting
10. Threatening to cause harm

:3HC_PinkDot: Social bullying- this involves hurting someone's relationships or reputation.

1. Ignoring or leaving someone out on purpose
2. Telling others not to be friends with someone else
3. Spreading rumours about someone
4. Destroying relationships and friendships
5. Embarrassing someone in public
6. Sharing information or images that will have a harmful effect on the other person
7. Telling awful lies or stories about someone to make others not like them anymore

Now that we have clarified what bullying is, it is important to explain why bullying is very harmful and very very bad to do that to someone else. 
When someone gets bullied on the internet which is referred to as Cyberbullying, it hurts their feelings and it makes them feel bad, and they can experience serious long lasting problems as a result of that. 

The victim of bullying will without exception experience sadness, despair, and anxiety. Depression or other serious mental health problems do often occur, and the victim might struggle with shame, low self esteem, and an inability to trust other people in future. They often experience negative physical, social, and mental health issues. They have increased feelings of loneliness and sadness, and have health complaints. They are also more likely to lose interest in the things they previously loved. Their sleeping patterns and eating patterns can change a lot, and they can some times experience insomnia and nighttime terrors. 

It is very important to be aware of the consequences which bullying can cause in someone else’s life, because if these symptoms go untreated then the victim might end up with poor academic performance, withdrawal from society and avoidance of social relationships, and in some cases the victim can end up bullying other people- in order to feel in control. 

But the worst case scenario is suicide. 
Rachael Neblett (17), and Ryan Patrick Halligan (13) are two teenagers that committed suicide, and their suicide has been directly connected to cyberbullying. Other similar cases have been documented. 
The percentages of individuals who have experienced cyberbullying at some point in their lifetimes have nearly doubled (18% to 34%) from 2007-2016.

Bullying is all around us. It is easy to be a bully and be mean to other people if you don’t understand the consequences of what it does to someone else. Bullies can tease, hurt, and even torment other people intentionally to make them feel bad and to hurt them. 

How can we help?

We all have to do our part to stop bullying. While identifying behavior is important, we should also take steps to stop it when it does occur by saying that it is wrong to do that, and say to the bully that what they are doing is hurtful and harmful.
